You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC task-86db697a evidence

This task was solved correctly on a fresh instance. Preserve the confirmed rule/evidence below, but do not overgeneralize it to every diagonal pair.

## Confirmed test transformation

The test had a uniform 8 field and a 2 diagonal pair at zero-based `(6,3)` and `(7,4)`, plus nearby 2/3/6 marks. The correct output added color 2 at `(5,2)`, `(4,1)`, `(3,0)`: extending the pair's down-right diagonal backward/up-left through the background until the grid edge. Every other cell, including the original 2, 3, and 6 marks, was preserved. This exact output was accepted.

## Demonstration evidence

- Demo 1 (background 0): multiple diagonal same-color pairs define diagonal extensions; lines are drawn through open background and original colored cells remain. Several directions and colors occur.
- Demo 2: unchanged 2x2 pattern `[[7,3],[5,7]]`; therefore “extend every adjacent equal-color diagonal pair” is not a universally valid rule.
- Demo 3: unchanged small boundary motif.
- Demo 4: unchanged; the diagonal 6 pair is bounded at one end by the grid edge and at the other by a different-color cell.
- Demo 5: diagonal lines of 6, 9, and 5 are extended through background from pairs; different-color cells/blockers and edges constrain them.
- Demo 6: multiple diagonal paths are extended for colors 4, 7, and 3, preserving the central seed motif.
- Demo 7: a diagonal 5 pair extends its open diagonal; another same-color diagonal is blocked immediately by a different color and gets no extension.

## Additional confirmed recurrence (background 9)

A fresh 10x25 test had 0s at zero-based `(7,10)`, `(8,9)`, and `(9,9)`, with unrelated 7 at `(8,8)` and 6 at `(9,8)`. Correct output extended the diagonal pair `(7,10)/(8,9)` up-right through `(6,11),(5,12),(4,13),(3,14),(2,15),(1,16),(0,17)`. Existing marks were preserved. This confirms extensions may proceed in either diagonal orientation; identify the qualifying diagonal pair and extend the open ray through background to the edge.

## Additional confirmed recurrence (background 7, 23x29)

A fresh 23x29 test had diagonal pairs: color 6 at `(9,2)/(10,3)`, color 2 at `(9,5)/(10,4)`, and color 0 at `(11,3)/(12,2)` (zero-based). Correct output extended each pair's exterior ray through background 7 to the nearest grid edge: 6 up-left from `(9,2)` to `(7,0)`; 2 up-right from `(9,5)` to `(0,14)`; 0 down-left from `(12,2)` to `(14,0)`. All original marks, including nearby 8 at `(11,4)`, were preserved. Accepted.

## Additional confirmed recurrence (background 6, 17x14)

Fresh test motif (1-based): color 3 at `(4,9)` and `(5,10)`; another nearby 3 at `(6,10)` is not part of that diagonal. The 3 pair's open up-left ray was extended through `(3,8),(2,7),(1,6)`. Color 7 at `(6,11)/(7,12)` extended down-right through `(8,13),(9,14)`. Nearby 4 at `(5,11)` and the other 3 at `(6,10)` were preserved. Accepted. Confirms one diagonal pair can be selected amid a small multi-color motif, and extensions proceed from its exterior endpoints through background to the edge.

## Additional demo evidence (background 9, 14x27)

A sparse vertical 8 motif at zero-based column 20, rows 10–13, with 0s at `(11,19)` and `(12,19)`, produced an up-right 8 ray from the upper endpoint `(10,20)`: `(9,21)` through `(4,26)`. The vertical source motif and adjacent 0s were preserved. This supports extending a task-selected open diagonal ray but does not justify extending arbitrary isolated marks or every diagonal-looking neighborhood.

## Additional accepted no-op recurrence (background 8, 10x25)

The input contained only a compact 2x2 mixed-color motif at rows 0–1, cols 9–10: `[[3,1],[2,5]]`; the rest was background 8. The correct output was unchanged. In particular, do not infer a diagonal extension from nearby different-color marks or promote colors based on proximity; when no qualifying same-color diagonal pair/ray is established, preserve the grid.

## Demo-request decision evidence

This instance's first demo showed a different geometry with a 4-cell vertical run of 8, two adjacent 0s, and an output diagonal 8 extension. It did not make the fresh 2×2 mixed-color motif a candidate for extension. An unchanged-output submission was accepted with no wrong attempts, confirming the importance of applicability checks and preserving the input if the demonstrated motif class is absent.

## Use on recurrences

1. Identify diagonal-adjacent equal-color pairs in the motif.
2. Check whether the corresponding diagonal rays are open; preserve all existing cells and stop at blockers/edges.
3. Do not extend a pair solely because it exists: Demo 2 is an explicit counterexample. Confirm motif/context or use an additional demo when competing interpretations predict different outputs.
4. For the confirmed test geometry, extend color 2 up-left from `(6,3)/(7,4)` through `(5,2),(4,1),(3,0)`.

## Additional confirmed recurrence (background 1, 18x22)

Fresh test motif (1-based): color 9 at `(9,4)/(10,5)`, color 6 at `(9,7)/(10,6)`, color 7 at `(11,5)/(12,4)`, plus unrelated color 2 at `(11,6)`. Correct output extended the open ray of each diagonal pair through background 1 to the edge, preserving all original cells: 9 continues up-left from `(9,4)` to `(6,1)`; 6 continues up-right from `(9,7)` to `(1,15)`; 7 continues down-left from `(12,4)` to `(15,1)`. Accepted. This confirms several pair rays can be extended simultaneously, including a pair adjacent to an unrelated distinct-color cell; only the ray path/blockers constrain the extension.

## Additional confirmed recurrence (background 7, 14x13)

Fresh test input had diagonal-adjacent equal-color pairs: color 6 at zero-based `(9,5)/(10,6)`; color 3 at `(9,8)/(10,7)`; color 0 at `(11,6)/(12,5)`; color 8 at `(11,7)/(12,8)`. Accepted after all four rays were included. The earlier incorrect attempts omitted the 0 ray and/or truncated the 3 ray, so audit all diagonal-adjacent pairs and extend the open outward ray fully to the boundary; do not omit a less salient pair.
